content:
As Amazon's Prime Day shopping festival takes place, with consumers searching for deals, many have discovered a rather interesting feature on the online retailer's website.

On Monday, user Megan Montgomery posted on Threads, sharing a screenshot of her account's "About You" page, writing: "I accidentally saw a page of Amazon's assumptions about me based on my shopping history, and I'm truly speechless."

Most of the content on the page consisted of mundane descriptions, such as "owns a Kindle Paperwhite," "has shopped in the women's department," and "hosts themed parties." However, Montgomery circled one hilarious assumption: "flat butt."

Amazon users can easily view their personal customer profiles. On the main page, hover your cursor over your name, select "Your Shopping Preferences," then click "About You." You can also hover over your name, click "Account," and then go to "About You."

According to Amazon's corporate news site, the "About You" feature launched in May this year, using artificial intelligence to infer users' personal information and preferences from multiple data sources, "including your conversations with the Alexa shopping assistant, product reviews you've written, your shopping history, items saved to lists, and your search history."

After Montgomery's post went viral, netizens joined in, sharing screenshots of their own pages—some of the assumptions were eerily accurate, some were hilariously absurd, and some could even be considered quite rude.

Although it appears the feature cannot be fully disabled, customers can manually update their pages (clearly, many have taken advantage of this in recent days, joining in the fun by sharing funny screenshots). However, the random details generated by Amazon's AI tool have already become incredibly hilarious.
